'''A highlighted run is wiki source: it comes back out verbatim. Edit around a token, never inside it.'''

==Copy from here==
Every token below is already formatted. Copy one into an article Doc and it keeps its highlight. House highlight colour: #FFF2CC (Highlight colour → Custom).

===Inline tokens 1–12===
#{for win,mac} … {/for} — OS / version conditional
#{note} … {/note}
#{warning} … {/warning}
#{key Ctrl+T} — keyboard shortcut
#{menu Account Settings} — menu path or label
#{button Add WebDAV} — button label
#{filepath prefs.js} — file name or path
#{pref mail.server.default} — preference
#[[Image:Name of screenshot]] — screenshot from the SUMO gallery
#[[Template:Sample]], [[Include:Sample]] — template
#[[How to Use Attachments]] — link to another KB article
#__TOC__, __NOTOC__ — magic words

===Block tokens 13–16, protected whole, line breaks included===
13. Table:
{|
! Provider !! Supported
|-
| WebDAV || yes
|}
14. Code block, two lines or more:
<code>
{
  "manifest_version": 2
}
</code>
15. HTML comment:

16. Leading indent / definition marker, where only the colon is the token:

:like this one

===Headings 1–4 — copy a whole line, then type over the text===
Headings are '''not''' tokens: the level lives in the paragraph's Doc style, so these four carry no highlight. Copy a whole line, paragraph mark included, and the level comes with it. Never highlight a heading — the highlight wins and the level is lost.

=Heading 1=
==Heading 2==
===Heading 3===
====Heading 4====

==Fine print — collapse this, expand it if something looks wrong==

===What survives an edit===
#Highlighted, any colour → back out '''verbatim''', as wiki source.
#Courier New with '''no''' highlight → an inline <code>code</code> span.
#Neither → ordinary prose; any wiki meaning is lost.

'''Any''' highlight colour counts — the check is only "does this run have a background colour". #FFF2CC is just the colour the tool applies, and one consistent colour is what makes "don't touch this" readable at a glance. Courier New is a visual cue only; the font is not part of the check.

Highlight a sentence by accident and it will be published as raw markup; delete a token's highlight and the article silently loses that construct. Adding a token by hand is fine: type the wiki text, then highlight it in #FFF2CC.

===Two habits===
*Leave a line that is '''nothing but tokens''' on its own line — that is how the article's structure survives the trip back.
*Don't tidy a token's spacing or capitalisation. It is source code, not prose.

===What is not a token===
Rendered as normal Doc formatting and converted back automatically: headings (Heading 1 is <code>=text=</code>, Heading 2 <code>==text==</code>, up to Heading 6 — most articles start at Heading 2), '''bold''', ''italic'', bulleted and numbered lists, external links, a single-line <code>code</code> span, and the inline HTML tags u, s, del, sub, sup, blockquote and br. Edit these like ordinary text. A '''single-line''' <code>like this</code> is '''not''' a token — it becomes real monospace formatting instead. A heading is the one construct a highlight can '''break''': highlight the whole line and it comes back as verbatim prose with its level gone. If you would rather type markup than use the style menu, put <code>==Heading==</code> in a '''normal''' paragraph and highlight that — it publishes as a heading, but the Doc no longer shows one, so the styled version above is the better habit.

A code block is preformatted on SUMO, so its line breaks and indentation are kept exactly. A comment starting <!-- TODO (sumo-kb-tools): --> is a note the tool left for you: act on it, then delete the comment before publishing.

One known limitation: a sub-bullet nested under a numbered step cannot be shown as a bullet by the Google Docs API, so it appears as a. / b. and converts back as a number. The tool leaves a TODO comment above any list where that happens.
